memory_update.text: CSTM is the strongest Layer 1B underfollowed candidate for automotive aluminum body sheet substitution because it has explicit auto body sheet products and North American production evidence.

STLD should be tracked as a reference capacity-expansion name because its Aluminum Dynamics project targets large-scale flat-rolled aluminum capacity including automotive applications, but qualification timing is the key gating factor.
KALU belongs in the underfollowed lane as a specialty aluminum processor with automotive exposure, but the evidence does not yet prove substitutability for exposed automotive body sheet.
Need primary evidence on OEM qualification lists, Ford/Lucid supplier diversification, and emergency allocation behavior after the Novelis Oswego outage.

The most important falsification test is whether automotive body sheet qualification is so application-specific that alternate public suppliers cannot absorb disrupted volumes within the relevant production window.

node: Automotive aluminum sheet and specialty rolling capacity
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow US-listed universe tied to automotive aluminum sheet and specialty rolling capacity. The clearest direct alternate-capacity candidate is Constellium, which publicly describes automotive body sheet products and North American auto-body-sheet production. Steel Dynamics is a large-cap reference/capacity-expansion name because its Aluminum Dynamics project targets flat-rolled aluminum for beverage, industrial, and automotive markets. Kaiser Aluminum is an underfollowed specialty aluminum processor with automotive exposure, but its exact substitutability for exposed automotive body sheet needs verification. Radius Recycling is a speculative second-order feedstock/recycling candidate, relevant only if aluminum scrap, closed-loop recycling, or toll-processing constraints become part of the outage-response chain.
